title: Aft Cargo Door Slow to Open in Cold Weather and Repeat Hydraulic Leaks
abstract: Cargo operator request to remove the hydraulic drive from the aft cargo door, following slow opening at northern European winter stations and a persistent leak rate at the door actuator that delays turnrounds.

sections.request: The aft cargo door is costing us turnround time at our northern stations. Below about minus ten degrees it takes nearly three times as long to open, and the loaders will not start until it is fully up and locked, so the whole turn slips. On top of that we are finding fluid in the door bay on roughly one aircraft in four at every check, and twice last winter we had to hold an aircraft on stand because the door would not close cleanly. Our ground staff have started opening the door manually as a matter of routine, which is not what we want them doing in the dark on an icy stand. We would like the hydraulic drive taken off this door altogether and replaced with something electric, if that is possible without a full door redesign.
sections.background: We operate nineteen aircraft in a scheduled freight pattern with an average of 2.4 turns per aircraft per day. Our records for the last two winters show 86 delays attributed to the aft cargo door, of which 61 were at stations below minus five degrees. The door bay leak findings run at 24 per cent of C checks. The hydraulic reservoir standard recommended by Aeralis was embodied on our whole fleet in 2022 and did not change the leak rate at the door.
sections.expected_outcome: An aft cargo door that opens to the same schedule at minus twenty degrees as it does at plus twenty, with no hydraulic fluid in the door bay, and with the change embodiable in two consecutive night stops rather than in a base visit.

type_data.business_justification: Eighty-six door-attributed departure delays over two winters on a nineteen-aircraft fleet, and a 24 per cent leak finding rate at C check on a component that is on the critical path of every turnround.
